Power Flow Analysis

Complete API for AC power flow analysis.

Quick Start

using Powerful, PowerFlowData

# Load system
case = PowerFlowData.parse_network("cases/ieee14.raw")
sys = SystemModel(case)

# Create problem and solve
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)  # Default: PowerInjection formulation
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())  # Fast native solver

# Access results
v = get_var(sol, :Bus, :v, 4001)  # Get voltage magnitude at bus 4001
θ = get_var(sol, :Bus, :θ, 4001)  # Get voltage angle

# Generate report
using DataFrames
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus)
df = DataFrame(bus_data)

Problem Definition & Solvers

Problem types, algorithms, and solution structures from solvers/.

Powerful.ACMethod — Type
ACMethod <: PowerFlowAlgorithm

Abstract type for AC power flow solution methods.

source
Powerful.ACPowerFlowProblem — Type
ACPowerFlowProblem <: PowerFlowProblem

AC power flow problem with full nonlinear equations.

Solves the nonlinear system g(y) = 0 where:

  • y contains bus voltage magnitudes and angles
  • g contains power balance equations at each bus

Automatically detects and handles multi-island systems when auto_split=true (default).

Fields

  • sys::Union{SystemModel, Vector{SystemModel}}: Power system (single or multi-island)
  • initial_guess::Union{Nothing, Vector{Float64}}: Starting point for iteration

Constructors

# Use system's current state as initial guess (default)
# Automatically detects islands
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)

# Provide custom initial guess
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys; initial_guess=y0)

# Disable auto-split for manual island handling
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys; auto_split=false)

Example

using Powerful

# Load and set up system
case = PowerFlowData.parse_network("cases/ieee14.raw")
sys = SystemModel(case)

# Create problem (auto-detects islands)
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)

# Solve with default algorithm
sol = solve(prob)  # Works for single or multi-island!

# Or specify algorithm
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson(abstol=1e-10))
source
Powerful.AlgorithmConfig — Type
AlgorithmConfig{M, S, B, L}

Full algorithm configuration composing all 5 levels.

Most users should use preset constructors like NewtonRaphson() or RobustNewton() instead of constructing this directly.

Type Parameters

  • M: Solution method type
  • S: Globalization strategy type
  • B: Implementation backend type
  • L: Linear solver type

Example (advanced users only)

# Full custom configuration
alg = AlgorithmConfig(
    NewtonRaphson(abstol=1e-10),
    NoGlobalization(),
    NativeBackend(),
    KLUSolver(ordering=:COLAMD)
)
sol = solve(prob, alg)
source
Powerful.CUDSSSolver — Type
CUDSSSolver <: LinearSolver

GPU sparse direct solver via CUDSS (CUDA Direct Sparse Solver).

Requires CUDA-capable GPU. Works in hybrid mode: CPU computes Jacobian, GPU performs factorization and triangular solves.

Usage

prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson(linear_solver=CUDSSSolver()))

Performance

Best for large systems (>10k buses) where GPU factorization speedup outweighs PCIe transfer overhead. Data transfers happen automatically each Newton iteration.

source
Powerful.DCPowerFlowProblem — Type
DCPowerFlowProblem <: PowerFlowProblem

DC power flow problem with linearized equations (future implementation).

Solves the linear system Ax = b where:

  • x contains bus voltage angles only
  • A is the DC admittance matrix (B' matrix)
  • b contains net power injections

Note

This is a placeholder for future implementation. DC power flow will be added when needed for contingency analysis and fast initial estimates.

source
Powerful.DishonestNewton — Type
DishonestNewton <: ACMethod

Dishonest Newton method with infrequent Jacobian updates (future).

Updates Jacobian every N iterations instead of every iteration. Trades convergence speed for reduced factorization cost.

Note

Useful for very large systems where Jacobian factorization dominates.

source
Powerful.FastDecoupled — Type
FastDecoupled <: ACMethod

Fast Decoupled Power Flow method with constant Jacobian matrices.

Exploits the weak coupling between P-θ and Q-V in power systems to use constant B' and B" matrices, factored once and reused across all iterations.

Variants

  • :XB - Traditional fast decoupled (neglects R, uses X only)
  • :BX - Alternate formulation (includes R effects)

Performance

2-3x faster than Newton-Raphson for well-conditioned transmission networks. Typical convergence: 10-20 iterations vs 3-5 for Newton (but smaller subsystems).

When to Use

✓ Large transmission networks (>1000 buses) ✓ Well-conditioned systems (high X/R ratio) ✓ Repeated solves (factorizations reused) ✗ Stressed systems near voltage collapse ✗ Distribution networks (low X/R ratio)

source
Powerful.GaussSeidel — Type
GaussSeidel <: ACMethod

Gauss-Seidel iterative method (future implementation).

Classic iterative method that solves one bus at a time. Primarily of historical/educational interest - much slower than Newton-Raphson.

source

Powerful.IterativeGMRES — Type
IterativeGMRES <: LinearSolver

Iterative GMRES solver (future implementation).

Useful for very large systems where direct factorization is too expensive. Requires good preconditioner for power system Jacobians.

source
Powerful.KLUSolver — Type
KLUSolver <: LinearSolver

Sparse LU factorization via KLU.jl with fill-reducing ordering.

KLU is optimized for circuit simulation and works excellently for power system Jacobians.

Ordering Options

  • :AMD - Approximate Minimum Degree (default, best for most cases)
  • :COLAMD - Column AMD (alternative)
  • :natural - No reordering (fastest factorization, but larger fill)

Fields

  • ordering::Symbol: Fill-reducing ordering strategy (default: :AMD)
source
Powerful.LinearSolver — Type
LinearSolver

Abstract type for linear system solvers (for J·Δy = -g in Newton method).

source
Powerful.MultiIslandSolution — Type
MultiIslandSolution{T}

Solution from power flow calculation on a multi-island system.

Transparent wrapper that makes multiple islands look like a single solution. Users can query variables using the same API as PowerFlowSolution.

Fields

  • islands::Vector{SystemModel}: Individual island systems
  • solutions::Vector{PowerFlowSolution{T}}: Per-island solutions
  • converged::Bool: True if ALL islands converged
  • iterations::Int: Maximum iterations across all islands
  • residual_norm::T: Maximum residual norm across all islands
  • retcode::Any: Aggregated return code
  • stats::Any: Aggregated statistics

Example

# Automatic island handling (recommended)
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)  # Auto-detects islands
sol = solve(prob, RobustNewton())

# Access works the same regardless of islands
v = get_var(sol, :Bus, :v, 4001)  # Finds correct island automatically
source
Powerful.NativeBackend — Type
NativeBackend <: ImplementationBackend

Use Powerful.jl's native Newton-Raphson implementation.

Optimized for power system problems with:

  • Sparse Jacobian with matrix coloring for ForwardDiff
  • KLU sparse factorization with fill-reducing ordering
  • Zero-allocation residual evaluation
  • Optional GPU acceleration

This is the recommended backend for most use cases.

source
Powerful.NoGlobalization — Type
NoGlobalization <: GlobalizationStrategy

No globalization - pure Newton steps.

Use when initial guess is good (e.g., flat start for well-conditioned systems).

source
Powerful.NonlinearSolveBackend — Type
NonlinearSolveBackend <: ImplementationBackend

Use NonlinearSolve.jl for robust solving with automatic algorithm selection.

Provides access to NonlinearSolve.jl's suite of algorithms:

  • Trust region methods
  • Levenberg-Marquardt
  • Pseudo-transient continuation
  • Automatic method selection

Recommended when native Newton fails or for research/comparison purposes.

CommonSolve.solve — Function
solve(prob::PowerFlowProblem, alg=default_algorithm(prob); kwargs...)

Solve a power flow problem with the specified algorithm.

This is the main entry point for the modern API. Matches the interface used by DifferentialEquations.jl, NonlinearSolve.jl, and Optimization.jl.

Arguments

  • prob::PowerFlowProblem: Problem to solve (e.g., ACPowerFlowProblem)
  • alg: Algorithm to use (defaults to problem-specific default)
  • kwargs...: Additional solver-specific options

Returns

Solution object with fields:

  • converged::Bool: Whether solver converged
  • iterations::Int: Number of iterations taken
  • residual_norm::Float64: Final residual norm
  • Additional fields depending on solver

Example

using Powerful

# Load system
case = PowerFlowData.parse_network("cases/ieee14.raw")
sys = SystemModel(case)

# Create problem
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)

# Solve with default algorithm
sol = solve(prob)

# Solve with specific algorithm
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson(abstol=1e-10))

# Solve with robust method
sol = solve(prob, RobustNewton())

# Check convergence
if sol.converged
    println("Converged in ", sol.iterations, " iterations")
    println("Final residual: ", sol.residual_norm)
else
    @warn "Did not converge"
end

See also: ACPowerFlowProblem, NewtonRaphson, RobustNewton

source
Powerful.FastDecoupledBX — Method
FastDecoupledBX(; kwargs...) -> AlgorithmConfig

Fast Decoupled Power Flow with BX formulation (includes resistance).

BX variant includes resistance effects: better for moderate X/R ratios.

Keyword Arguments

  • max_iter::Int=100: Maximum iterations
  • abstol::Float64=1e-6: Convergence tolerance
  • ordering::Symbol=:AMD: KLU ordering

Example

prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection())
sol = solve(prob, FastDecoupledBX())
source
Powerful.FastDecoupledXB — Method
FastDecoupledXB(; kwargs...) -> AlgorithmConfig

Fast Decoupled Power Flow with XB formulation (neglects resistance).

XB variant uses susceptance-only approximation: B'[i,j] = -bij = -Im(Yij). Best for transmission networks with high X/R ratio.

Keyword Arguments

  • max_iter::Int=100: Maximum iterations (FDPF typically needs 2-4x more than Newton)
  • abstol::Float64=1e-6: Convergence tolerance on max(|ΔP|, |ΔQ|)
  • ordering::Symbol=:AMD: KLU fill-reducing ordering (:AMD, :COLAMD, :natural)

Example

prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection())
sol = solve(prob, FastDecoupledXB())  # 2-3x faster than Newton for large systems

# Tighter tolerance
sol = solve(prob, FastDecoupledXB(abstol=1e-8, max_iter=50))
source
Powerful.NewtonRaphson — Method
NewtonRaphson(; kwargs...) -> AlgorithmConfig

Fast native Newton-Raphson with KLU sparse solver (recommended default).

Keyword Arguments

  • max_iter::Int=50: Maximum iterations
  • abstol::Float64=1e-8: Convergence tolerance on ||g||∞
  • reltol::Float64=1e-8: Relative tolerance (currently unused, for future use)
  • ordering::Symbol=:AMD: KLU fill-reducing ordering (:AMD, :COLAMD, :natural)
  • linear_solver::Union{Nothing, LinearSolver}=nothing: Override linear solver (e.g., CUDSSSolver())

Algorithm Stack

  • Method: Newton-Raphson (full Jacobian, quadratic convergence)
  • Globalization: None (pure Newton steps)
  • Backend: Native (Powerful.jl's optimized implementation)
  • Linear solver: KLU with AMD ordering (default), or user-specified

Example

prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)

# Use defaults (abstol=1e-8, max_iter=50, AMD ordering)
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())

# Tighter tolerance for sensitivity analysis
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson(abstol=1e-12))

# More iterations for difficult cases
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson(max_iter=100))

# Try different ordering
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson(ordering=:COLAMD))

# Use GPU linear solver (requires CUDA + CUDSS)
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson(linear_solver=CUDSSSolver()))
source
Powerful.RobustNewton — Method
RobustNewton(; kwargs...) -> AlgorithmConfig

Robust Newton via NonlinearSolve.jl with automatic algorithm selection.

Uses NonlinearSolve.jl's default algorithm which automatically selects trust region, Levenberg-Marquardt, or other robust methods based on problem characteristics.

Keyword Arguments

  • max_iter::Int=50: Maximum iterations
  • abstol::Float64=1e-8: Convergence tolerance
  • reltol::Float64=1e-8: Relative tolerance (currently unused, for future use)

Algorithm Stack

  • Method: Newton-Raphson (interface to NonlinearSolve)
  • Globalization: Automatic (trust region, line search, etc.)
  • Backend: NonlinearSolve.jl
  • Linear solver: Automatic (typically KLU)

When to Use

  • Native Newton fails to converge
  • Poor initial guess (e.g., high-load stressed systems)
  • Research/comparison purposes
  • Exploring NonlinearSolve.jl's features

Example

prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)

# Robust solver (slower but more reliable)
sol = solve(prob, RobustNewton())

# Compare with native Newton
sol_native = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())
sol_robust = solve(prob, RobustNewton())
source
Powerful.apply_addressing_strategy! — Method
apply_addressing_strategy!(am::AddressManager, sys::SystemModel, formulation::FormulationTrait)

Apply AMD or custom permutation reordering to addresses.

This function handles address reordering strategies that require sparsity analysis, which is only available after setup_with_formulation! has assigned basic addresses.

Must be called after setup_with_formulation!.

Supported Strategies

  • NaturalAddressing: No-op (addresses remain in natural order)
  • AMDAddressing: Computes sparsity pattern, AMD permutation, and remaps addresses
  • CustomPermutation: Applies user-provided permutation

Example

am = AddressManager(strategy=AMDAddressing())
setup_with_formulation!(am, sys, formulation)      # Basic addresses
apply_addressing_strategy!(am, sys, formulation)   # AMD reordering

Powerful.NewtonWorkspace — Type
NewtonWorkspace{SYS, JT, BT, PT}

Pre-allocated workspace for Newton-Raphson power flow solver.

Separates one-time setup (sparsity detection, coloring, allocation) from allocation-free Newton iterations. Uses plain vectors for iteration state, eliminating aliasing issues and ensuring zero allocations in the hot loop.

Type Parameters

  • SYS: SystemModel type (matches CachedAutodiffWorkspace)
  • JT: Jacobian type (SparseMatrixCSC or Matrix)
  • BT: Backend type for differentiation (AutoSparse or Nothing)
  • PT: Prep type for Jacobian (PreparedJacobian or Nothing)

Fields

  • cache::CachedAutodiffWorkspace{SYS}: Residual evaluator
  • iter_dae::DAE{Vector{Float64}}: Current iteration state (y, g)
  • ls_dae::DAE{Vector{Float64}}: Line search trial state (yls, gls)
  • dy::Vector{Float64}: Newton update direction (RHS buffer)
  • J::Union{Matrix, SparseMatrixCSC}: Jacobian matrix
  • jac_prep: Prepared Jacobian (coloring, etc.)
  • jac_backend: Differentiation backend
  • use_sparse::Bool: Use sparse Jacobian
  • use_gpu::Bool: Use GPU linear solver
  • solver_fact::Base.RefValue: Cached factorization (KLU or CUDSS)

Example

# One-time setup (expensive: sparsity, coloring, allocation)
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)
workspace = setup_powerflow_newton(prob; use_sparse=true, verbose=true)

# Solve multiple times with different initial conditions (allocation-free!)
y0_1 = copy(workspace.iter_dae.y)
sol1 = solve_powerflow_newton!(workspace, y0_1; abstol=1e-8)

y0_2 = y0_1 .* 1.1  # Different initial guess
sol2 = solve_powerflow_newton!(workspace, y0_2; abstol=1e-10)

# Benchmark iterations only (no setup overhead)
@btime solve_powerflow_newton!($workspace, $y0_1; abstol=1e-8, verbose=false)

Design Notes

Power flow solves algebraic equations only. When state variables (x, f) are added for dynamic simulation, they will be added as explicit fields to this workspace or a separate DynamicSimWorkspace will be created.

source
Powerful.PowerFlowSolution — Type
PowerFlowSolution{T}

Solution from a power flow calculation.

Fields

  • converged::Bool: Whether the solver converged
  • y::Vector{T}: Final algebraic variables (voltages, angles)
  • residual_norm::T: Final residual norm (infinity norm)
  • iterations::Int: Number of Newton iterations
  • retcode: Return code from NonlinearSolve
  • stats: Additional solver statistics
  • prob::PROB: ACPowerFlowProblem (contains sys, address_manager, formulation)
  • _generator_residuals::Base.RefValue: Lazy cache for generator contributions (internal)

Generator Contributions Cache

The _generator_residuals field caches generator reactive power contributions computed after power flow converges. Access via get_generator_residuals(sol) which lazily evaluates on first access. The cache allows efficient repeated queries without re-evaluation.

DAE Reference

The dae field stores a reference to the workspace DAE from the solver. This enables efficient variable copying for TDS initialization via copy_pf_variables_by_key! without code duplication. Since it's a reference, memory overhead is minimal (~8 bytes).

source

Powerful.get_generator_residuals — Method
get_generator_residuals(sol::PowerFlowSolution{T}) where T

Lazy accessor for generator residual contributions after power flow converges.

Returns residual vector containing actual power injections from generators (PV and Slack) that were computed by running residual evaluation in "observation mode" (force_accumulate=true).

Physical Interpretation

For converged power flow, this function extracts:

  • PV generators: Actual Q injection at bus to maintain voltage V = Vs
  • Slack generators: Actual P and Q injections to maintain voltage and angle

The residuals are evaluated with generators accumulating (not replacing) bus power balance equations, allowing extraction of their actual contributions.

Returns

  • Vector{T}: Residual vector of same length as solution, with generator contributions at bus injection positions. Non-generator positions contain load/branch contributions.

Caching Behavior

  • First call: Computes generator residuals and caches result
  • Subsequent calls: Returns cached result (O(1) operation)

Example

prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())

# Extract generator contributions (computed and cached on first call)
g_gen = get_generator_residuals(sol)

# Access PV reactive power at specific bus
q_addrs = get_addresses(sol.prob.address_manager, :Bus, :q_inj)
q_gen_bus5 = g_gen[q_addrs[5]]

See Also

  • evaluate_generator_contributions!: Direct evaluation without caching
source

Powerful.setup_powerflow — Method
setup_powerflow(sys::SystemModel; kwargs...) -> NonlinearSolveWorkspace

Perform all one-time setup for NonlinearSolve.jl-based power flow solver.

This function separates setup cost from iteration cost, enabling:

  • Precise benchmarking of iterations only
  • Reusing workspace for multiple solves with different initial conditions
  • Clear visibility into setup vs iteration allocation

Arguments

  • sys::SystemModel: Configured system model (must be set up with setup!)

Keyword Arguments

  • use_sparse::Bool=true: Use sparse Jacobian with coloring
  • solver=nothing: NonlinearSolve algorithm (default: TrustRegion)
  • autodiff=nothing: Automatic differentiation backend (for dense mode)
  • verbose::Bool=false: Print detailed setup progress

Returns

  • NonlinearSolveWorkspace: Pre-allocated workspace ready for repeated solves

Example

using PowerFlowData
using Powerful

# Load system
case = PowerFlowData.parse_network("cases/ieee14.raw")
sys = SystemModel(case)

# One-time setup with timing details
workspace = setup_powerflow(sys; use_sparse=true, verbose=true)

# Multiple solves (fast, no setup overhead!)
y0 = copy(workspace.iter_dae.y)
sol1 = solve_powerflow!(workspace, y0; abstol=1e-8)
sol2 = solve_powerflow!(workspace, y0; abstol=1e-10)

# Benchmark iterations precisely (excludes setup)
using BenchmarkTools
@btime solve_powerflow!($workspace, $y0; abstol=1e-8)

See Also

  • solve_powerflow!: Solve using pre-allocated workspace
  • solve_powerflow: Convenience wrapper (setup + solve)
  • setup_powerflow_newton: Hand-baked Newton solver setup
source
Powerful.setup_powerflow_newton — Method
setup_powerflow_newton(prob::ACPowerFlowProblem; kwargs...) -> NewtonWorkspace

Perform all one-time setup for Newton-Raphson power flow solver.

This function separates setup cost from iteration cost, enabling:

  • Precise benchmarking of iterations only
  • Reusing workspace for multiple solves with different initial conditions
  • Clear visibility into setup vs iteration allocation

Arguments

  • prob::ACPowerFlowProblem: Power flow problem with system, formulation, and address manager

Keyword Arguments

  • use_sparse::Bool=true: Use sparse Jacobian with coloring
  • use_gpu::Bool=false: Use GPU linear solver (requires use_sparse=true)
  • klu_ordering::Int=0: KLU ordering (0=AMD default, 1=COLAMD, 2=natural/no permutation)
  • verbose::Bool=false: Print detailed setup progress

Returns

  • NewtonWorkspace: Pre-allocated workspace ready for allocation-free iterations

Example

# Create power flow problem with formulation
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection())

# One-time setup with timing details
workspace = setup_powerflow_newton(prob; use_sparse=true, verbose=true)

# Multiple solves (fast, no setup overhead!)
sol1 = solve_powerflow_newton!(workspace, initial_guess_1; abstol=1e-8)
sol2 = solve_powerflow_newton!(workspace, initial_guess_2; abstol=1e-10)

# Benchmark iterations precisely (excludes setup)
using BenchmarkTools
y0 = copy(workspace.iter_dae.y)
@btime solve_powerflow_newton!($workspace, $y0; abstol=1e-8, verbose=false)

See Also

  • solve_powerflow_newton!: Allocation-free iteration function
  • solve: High-level API with algorithm presets
  • NewtonWorkspace: Workspace structure documentation

Powerful.solve_powerflow! — Method
solve_powerflow!(workspace::NonlinearSolveWorkspace, initial_guess::Vector; kwargs...)
    -> PowerFlowSolution

Solve power flow using pre-allocated NonlinearSolve workspace.

This function performs ONLY the solve, assuming all setup has been done via setup_powerflow. This enables precise benchmarking and efficient repeated solves.

Arguments

  • workspace::NonlinearSolveWorkspace: Pre-allocated workspace from setup_powerflow
  • initial_guess::Vector: Initial guess for algebraic variables

Keyword Arguments

  • abstol::Real=1e-8: Absolute tolerance for residual norm
  • reltol::Real=1e-8: Relative tolerance
  • maxiters::Int=50: Maximum iterations
  • solver=nothing: Override default solver (from workspace)

Returns

  • PowerFlowSolution: Solution object with convergence status and results

Example

# One-time setup
workspace = setup_powerflow(sys; use_sparse=true)

# Get initial guess
y0 = copy(workspace.iter_dae.y)

# Solve with different tolerances (fast, no setup overhead!)
sol_loose = solve_powerflow!(workspace, y0; abstol=1e-6)
sol_tight = solve_powerflow!(workspace, y0; abstol=1e-10)

# Try different initial conditions
y0_perturbed = y0 .* 1.05  # 5% perturbation
sol_perturbed = solve_powerflow!(workspace, y0; abstol=1e-8)

# Benchmark iterations only (excludes setup)
using BenchmarkTools
@btime solve_powerflow!($workspace, $y0; abstol=1e-8)

See Also

  • setup_powerflow: One-time setup function
  • solve_powerflow: Convenience wrapper (setup + solve)
  • solve_powerflow_newton!: Hand-baked Newton solver
source
Powerful.solve_powerflow_newton! — Method
solve_powerflow_newton!(workspace::NewtonWorkspace, initial_guess::Vector; kwargs...)
    -> PowerFlowSolution

Solve power flow using pre-allocated workspace (allocation-free iterations).

This function performs ONLY Newton-Raphson iterations, assuming all setup has been done via setup_powerflow_newton. All buffers are pre-allocated, making this suitable for:

  • Precise iteration benchmarks (excludes setup overhead)
  • Multiple solves with different initial conditions
  • Repeated solves in optimization loops

Arguments

  • workspace::NewtonWorkspace: Pre-allocated workspace from setup_powerflow_newton
  • initial_guess::Vector: Initial guess for all variables. IMPORTANT: Must be a copy of workspace.iter_dae.y or your custom guess. Do NOT pass the workspace vector directly as it will be mutated during iterations

Keyword Arguments

  • abstol::Real=1e-8: Absolute tolerance for residual norm
  • maxiters::Int=50: Maximum Newton iterations
  • damping::Real=1.0: Step size damping factor (0.5 for cautious, 1.0 for full Newton)
  • verbose::Bool=false: Print iteration details with timing

Returns

  • PowerFlowSolution: Solution object with convergence status and results

Example

# One-time setup
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)
workspace = setup_powerflow_newton(prob; use_sparse=true, verbose=true)

# IMPORTANT: Copy the initial guess (workspace vectors are mutated during solve)
y0 = copy(workspace.iter_dae.y)

# Solve with different tolerances (fast, no setup overhead!)
sol_loose = solve_powerflow_newton!(workspace, y0; abstol=1e-6)
sol_tight = solve_powerflow_newton!(workspace, y0; abstol=1e-10)

# Try different initial conditions
y0_perturbed = y0 .* 1.05  # 5% perturbation
sol_perturbed = solve_powerflow_newton!(workspace, y0_perturbed; abstol=1e-8)

# Benchmark iterations only (excludes setup)
using BenchmarkTools
@btime solve_powerflow_newton!($workspace, $y0; abstol=1e-8, verbose=false)

Notes

  • Uses DAE accessor functions to be future-proof when state variables are added
  • All iteration buffers pre-allocated in workspace (allocation-free after warmup)
  • Linear solver factorization cached and reused across iterations

See Also

  • setup_powerflow_newton: One-time setup function
  • solve: High-level API (recommended for most users)
  • NewtonWorkspace: Workspace structure documentation

Powerful.FastDecoupledWorkspace — Type
FastDecoupledWorkspace{PROB, AT, BT}

Pre-allocated workspace for allocation-free Fast Decoupled Power Flow.

All buffers allocated during setup, iterations are allocation-free.

Type Parameters

  • PROB: ACPowerFlowProblem type
  • AT: Array type (Vector{Float64} or CuArray)
  • BT: B-matrix type (SparseMatrixCSC)

Fields

  • prob::PROB: Power flow problem (sys, address_manager, formulation)
  • adcache::ADCache: Residual evaluator for mismatch computation
  • iter_dae::DAE{AT}: Current iteration state (θ, V in y vector)
  • B_prime::BT: Constant P-θ coupling matrix
  • B_double_prime::BT: Constant Q-V coupling matrix
  • lu_Bp::RefValue: Cached KLU factorization of B'
  • lu_Bpp::RefValue: Cached KLU factorization of B"
  • mismatch_P::AT: Active power mismatch buffer (ΔP)
  • mismatch_Q::AT: Reactive power mismatch buffer (ΔQ)
  • rhs_P::AT: Right-hand side for P-θ solve (ΔP/V)
  • rhs_Q::AT: Right-hand side for Q-V solve (ΔQ/V)
  • delta_theta::AT: Angle correction (output buffer)
  • delta_V::AT: Voltage magnitude correction (output buffer)
  • variant::Symbol: :XB or :BX
  • pq_bus_indices::Vector{Int}: Internal indices of PQ buses
  • pv_bus_indices::Vector{Int}: Internal indices of PV buses
  • slack_bus_index::Int: Internal index of slack bus
  • theta_addrs::Vector{UInt64}: DAE addresses for θ variables
  • v_addrs::Vector{UInt64}: DAE addresses for V variables
  • P_res_addrs::Vector{UInt64}: DAE addresses for P residuals
  • Q_res_addrs::Vector{UInt64}: DAE addresses for Q residuals

Powerful.setup_powerflow_fastdecoupled — Method
setup_powerflow_fastdecoupled(prob::ACPowerFlowProblem; kwargs...)
    -> FastDecoupledWorkspace

One-time setup for Fast Decoupled Power Flow with allocation-free iterations.

Constructs and factors B' and B" matrices once. All subsequent iterations reuse these factorizations with zero allocations.

Arguments

  • prob::ACPowerFlowProblem: Power flow problem (must use PowerInjection formulation)

Keyword Arguments

  • variant::Symbol=:XB: Variant (:XB neglects R, :BX includes R)
  • klu_ordering::Int=0: KLU ordering (0=AMD, 1=COLAMD, 2=natural)
  • verbose::Bool=false: Print setup progress

Returns

  • FastDecoupledWorkspace: Pre-allocated workspace for allocation-free iterations

Example

prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection())
workspace = setup_powerflow_fastdecoupled(prob; variant=:XB, verbose=true)

y0 = copy(workspace.iter_dae.y)
sol = solve_powerflow_fastdecoupled!(workspace, y0; abstol=1e-6)

Performance

Setup cost is amortized over iterations:

  • Setup: ~5-10ms (one-time)
  • Iteration: ~1-2ms (allocation-free)

For repeated solves, workspace can be reused with different initial conditions.

Powerful.solve_powerflow_fastdecoupled! — Method
solve_powerflow_fastdecoupled!(workspace::FastDecoupledWorkspace, initial_guess; kwargs...)
    -> PowerFlowSolution

Solve power flow using Fast Decoupled method with zero allocations per iteration.

All buffers pre-allocated in workspace, factorizations reused across iterations.

Arguments

  • workspace: Pre-allocated workspace from setup_powerflow_fastdecoupled
  • initial_guess: Initial guess for variables (θ, V)

Keyword Arguments

  • abstol::Real=1e-4: Absolute tolerance on max(|ΔP|, |ΔQ|)
  • maxiters::Int=100: Maximum iterations
  • verbose::Bool=false: Print iteration progress

Returns

  • PowerFlowSolution: Solution with convergence status

Example

workspace = setup_powerflow_fastdecoupled(prob; variant=:XB)
y0 = copy(workspace.iter_dae.y)

# Allocation-free solve
sol = solve_powerflow_fastdecoupled!(workspace, y0; abstol=1e-6)

# Benchmark iterations only (no setup overhead)
using BenchmarkTools
@btime solve_powerflow_fastdecoupled!($workspace, $y0; abstol=1e-6, verbose=false)
